text_blocks.snippet: Losartan (Cozaar) is a prescription medication used to treat high blood pressure and protect kidney function, and while generally well-tolerated, it can cause both mild and serious side effects.
These symptoms are usually mild and tend to improve over time as your body adjusts to the medication:

list.snippet: Dizziness or lightheadedness (caused by lowering blood pressure, especially when standing up quickly)
Upper respiratory tract infections or cold symptoms (stuffy nose, sneezing, sore throat)
Digestive issues (mild nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea)

text_blocks.snippet: Contact a healthcare professional or seek emergency care immediately if you experience severe reactions:

list.snippet: Allergic reactions (Angioedema): Sudden swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or trouble breathing and swallowing.
High potassium (Hyperkalemia): Can cause muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat, or chest pain.
Kidney problems: Signs include a dramatic decrease in urination, swelling in the legs, ankles, or feet, and severe fatigue.
Severe low blood pressure (Hypotension): Fainting, confusion, or severe dizziness.
Pregnancy warning: Do not take losartan if you are pregnant, as it can cause serious injury or death to an unborn baby.

text_blocks.snippet: You can read more comprehensive prescribing details via the Mayo Clinic Losartan Guide.
